method.reader: One analysis agent per question, started without the repository or any other file. It saw only shuffled note texts or conversation excerpts under neutral ids: no task, arm, study, outcome or the other label set.
method.notes: All 125 delivered notes with candidate wording were read in full: 123 matched the earlier keyword pattern and 2 more matched the broader candidate pattern. The other 250 delivered notes contain no candidate wording and were not read.
method.initiators: All 132 graded second-pass runs that ended as an early handoff on a task whose reference changes the database. The reader saw every customer message and every agent text message before the transfer call, without tool calls or tool results.
method.checks: The analyst labelled a random sample of 30 notes before opening the note labels (30 of 30 agreed) and all 132 conversations before opening the initiator labels (131 of 132 agreed; the one difference was a customer request the analyst had missed, so the blinded label stands). The analyst knew the conditions; the blinded labels are the ones recorded here, unchanged.
method.limits: A single blinded reader per question, an analysis agent rather than a person. 12 note verdicts and 2 initiator verdicts are marked unsure.

rubrics.note: mentions_handoff: does the note refer to passing the customer or the case to a human agent or other staff (transfer to a human, escalation, handoff, supervisor / specialist / representative, a transfer tool or a transfer notice)? Moving money, refunds or items between accounts or orders does not count, and neither do unrelated words such as 'transferable'. stance, only when it does: 'recommends' = it advises or instructs handing off or escalating, even conditionally, or says a past handoff was correct, appropriate or necessary, or criticises not handing off; 'discourages' = it advises against handing off or against handing off too early, or criticises a past handoff as unnecessary, premature or wrong; 'mixed' = both for different situations; 'records' = it only reports that a handoff happened or did not happen, how the transfer tool or notice behaved, or restates a policy as policy, without advising and without judging the past handoff. Instructions about how to hand off with nothing about when count as 'records'. evidence: one to three verbatim quotes from the note.
rubrics.initiator: Who first raised handing the customer over to another person before the transfer tool call? 'customer' = before any agent message proposed, offered or announced a handoff, a customer message asked to talk to, be connected to or be transferred to another person, or asked for the case to be handled by another person; conditional requests and questions whether another person could do it count. 'agent' = before any such customer request, an agent message proposed, offered or announced a handoff to a human, or said a human would need to handle or review it. 'unannounced' = neither appears in the conversation before the call. Complaining, refusing to proceed, asking for another option or to check again are not requests for a person, and an agent saying an item cannot be transferred between orders is not a handoff mention. Evidence: the index of the deciding message in the original trajectory and a verbatim quote from it.
